findings.title: Nil dereference when unsubscribing without an existing TopicUser record
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user has never visited or interacted with the topic (for example, a user receiving notifications via mailing list mode without a pre-existing `TopicUser` row, or visiting `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` directly). Accessing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`. In addition, when `tu` is mutated before `perform_show_response`, `@topic_view` has already been initialized and memoized its `@topic_user` on line 99, so the serialized `TopicView` preloaded into the page will still report the old notification level to the client unless `TopicView` is instantiated after updating `TopicUser` (or `TopicUser.change` is used prior to creating `TopicView`).

findings.title: Unsubscribing via GET mutates state on link preloading or crawlers and bypasses TopicUser.change
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is exposed on `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and immediately mutates the user's notification level on the GET request. Moreover, because it toggles `watching`/`tracking` down to `regular`, and `regular` down to `muted`, a second GET request (for example from an email client/browser link prefetcher, anti-virus scanner, or the user refreshing the page) will unexpectedly downgrade the topic from `regular` to `muted`. Also, updating `tu.notification_level` directly with `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, and the MessageBus notification level update are not recorded.
